XXFORESTTEXT: Table~\ref{tab:capgrid} reports the exact ratio for caps 2, 3 and 4. At cap three the best pre-committed design needs a median 1.51 times as many records as the best branching design (maximum 1.85), and the ratio grows from 1.38 at $m=6$ to 1.64 at $m=12$. The medians at caps 2 and 4 are 1.31 and 1.24. Designs fitted on training records realize ratios within a median 3\% of the exact ones on the same tasks at every cap. Branching restricted to the forests\textquotesingle{} own trees captures a median of only 17\% of the log-gain at cap three: the optimal branching designs mix many trees that neither forest contains.
XXSCREENTEXT: Table~\ref{tab:screening} shows that the gain depends on how many questions the screening decision needs. On BRFSS the best pre-committed design needs a median of 1.35--1.58 times as many respondents at caps 4 to 6. One more round removes most of this cost: at caps 4, 5 and 6 (at $b=6$ for 1 of the six trees) the exact optimal two-round design needs a median 1.00 times as many, recovering a median 100\% of the log-gap and at least 90\% in each of the 13 runs with a gain, against 33\%--63\% for following the root question and then a fixed form. Over the 21 runs with a gain, the optimized path-set design of Proposition~\ref{prop:uppermain} is within a median 2.0\% (at most 3.9\%) of the best fixed design, so the bracket between the lower end and this upper end is narrow and computable from reference data, whereas the completion-only end $N_P$ overstates the loss by a median factor 4.3. On thyroid every tree, up to depth six, depends on at most $b$ items, so $\Gamma_P=1$ and pre-commitment costs nothing intrinsic; the lower end detects this from reference data, and the rule \emph{reference lower end at most 1.05 $\Rightarrow$ no material gain} has no misses over all screening runs and forest tasks (Appendix~\ref{app:capsens}).
XXSCALETEXT: With all 21 BRFSS variables the profile cube has $2^{21}$ elements and the form program has 1,330 forms at $b=3$ and 5,985 forms at $b=4$; the solver certifies the optimal fixed design without enumerating the cube, in a median of 6 minutes at $b=4$ on one core. At $b=3$ every tree depends on at most $b$ items, so $\Gamma_P=1$ and there is no gain. At $b=4$ the best pre-committed design needs a median 1.46 times as many respondents (maximum 1.55), the fitted design 1.54, and the optimized path-set end lies at 1.50 (Table~\ref{tab:screening}, Appendix~\ref{app:scale}).
XXSHIFTTEXT: Imputation from complete source records uses information that the capped audit does not collect, and it is only as good as the transport of the conditional law of unasked items. When that law transports, as under the random-half and sex splits, regression imputation and multiple imputation attain RMSE 0.89--0.99 times that of branching with coverage 0.940--0.993, and they are the better tool. Under the education shift at both caps and the poor-health shift at $b=5$, regression imputation is biased by up to 1.73 branching standard deviations and covers 0.515--0.902 of the time, multiple imputation covers 0.667--0.935, and branching and the fitted fixed form stay unbiased with coverage 0.940--0.960. Under the cost-barrier shift at both caps and the poor-health shift at $b=4$ imputation stays close to nominal (bias at most 0.23 standard deviations). The design-based scores need neither the reference nor the transport assumption, and that is the setting in which within-record adaptivity matters (Table~\ref{tab:shift}).
XXORDERTEXT: If the last of $b$ answers flips with probability $0.1$ and earlier ones proportionally less often, both designs are biased: on BRFSS the median absolute bias at $n=1000$ is 1.54 clean branching standard errors for branching and 2.17 for the fitted fixed form, comparable to the sampling gains above, and branching keeps the smaller RMSE in 24 of 24 runs (Appendix~\ref{app:measurement}).
XXORDER: in the position model of Section~\ref{sec:experiments}, a 10\% chance that the last answer flips biases branching and form scores by a median 1.54 and 2.17 branching standard errors at $n=1000$.

XXFORESTPROFILES: At $m=12$ the held-out records occupy a median of 171, 388 and 121 of the 4,096 profiles for WDBC, Spambase and Ionosphere (ranges 164--180, 373--405 and 113--130 over twenty splits). Spambase, whose 3,101 held-out records cover few profiles densely, gives a median exact ratio of 1.58 at $b=3$, $m=12$, close to WDBC (1.66) and Ionosphere (1.73), so the gains are not an artifact of sparse held-out sets; Appendix~\ref{app:capsens} also varies the smoothing mass and resamples the held-out records.
XXFORESTCERT: At $b\in\{4,5\}$ column generation stops when the certified bounds agree to relative error $10^{-4}$ or no tree improves the master; over the 15 tasks computed with the new solver the largest relative gap of the reported ratio is 2e-08, the median number of iterations 28 and the median time 40 seconds per task on one core. At $b\in\{2,3\}$ the dense implementation certified every task to $10^{-6}$.
XXCOST: For the BRFSS trees ($m=12$) the median $\rho$ is 1.49, 1.35, 1.58 at $b=4, 5, 6$, so complete records undercut the best fixed design once a label costs more than about 12, 15, 4 feature questions, respectively, while branching is never undercut. Under an immutable cap the complete-record alternative is unavailable.
XXABSTRACT: In exact computations on random-forest updates and on screening trees with up to 21 survey items, pre-commitment costs a factor between one and 1.98 in records, an optimal second round of questions recovers most of it, and imputation from complete source records is preferable when its transport assumption holds but loses coverage under pre-specified population shifts.
XXCONTRIBEXP: Certified constants for forest updates at caps two to four and for screening trees on 12 and 21 survey items: pre-commitment costs a factor between one and 1.98, the exact optimal two-round design recovers a median 100\% of the log-gap on BRFSS at caps four and five and six, the path-set upper end is within a median 2.0\% of the optimum, and under pre-specified population shifts imputation from complete source records loses coverage while design-based scores keep it.
XXDISCUSSION: Exact computations show that ordinary models realize gains between one and 1.98 at caps of two to six, that an optimal second round recovers most of that gain on screening trees, that the bracket computed from reference data is narrow enough to plan with, and that branching designs restricted to the models\textquotesingle{} own trees miss most of the gain.
